title: Spectra: Multi-Scale Implicit Decomposition for Deepfake Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.31979v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deepfakes increasingly undermine trust in digital media, yet existing detectors often struggle to generalize across unseen manipulation techniques, compression levels, and dataset shifts. Most approaches rely on RGB appearance, frequency-domain artifacts, or their combination, learning cues present in the final synthesized image. While effective in-distribution, such cues are frequently generator-specific and can diminish as synthesis models evolve. We argue that a complementary perspective can be obtained through implicit neural representations (INRs), which expose how an image is reconstructed rather than merely how it appears. By fitting an INR to an image and analyzing its internal activations, one can reveal reconstruction dynamics that are difficult to observe in the image domain alone and may capture more intrinsic differences between genuine and synthetic content. To this end, we propose Spectra, a deepfake detection framework

translated_title: Spectra：面向深度伪造检测的多尺度隐式分解方法
translated_abstract: 深度伪造日益破坏人们对数字媒体的信任，然而现有检测器往往难以在未见过的伪造技术、压缩程度和数据集偏移上实现泛化。大多数方法依赖于RGB外观、频域伪影或二者的结合，学习的是最终合成图像中存在的线索。这类线索虽然在分布内有效，但通常是针对特定生成器的，并会随着合成模型的演进而逐渐失效。我们认为，隐式神经表示（INRs）可以提供一种互补的视角，它揭示的是图像如何被重构，而不仅仅是图像的外观。通过将INR拟合到图像并分析其内部激活，可以揭示仅凭图像域难以观察到的重构动态，并可能捕捉到真实内容与合成内容之间更本质的差异。为此，我们提出了Spectra，一个深度伪造检测框架（原文摘要至此处截断）。
tldr: Spectra通过将隐式神经表示拟合到图像并分析其多尺度内部激活，揭示图像的重构动态，从而捕捉真实与合成内容之间更本质的差异，克服了传统基于外观或频域线索的方法在泛化性上的局限。
en_tdlr: Spectra is a deepfake detection framework that fits implicit neural representations (INRs) to images and analyzes their multi-scale internal activations, revealing reconstruction dynamics that capture intrinsic differences between real and synthetic content and improving generalization over appearance- or frequency-based cues.
